increments.title: The collector accepts, keeps, persists, serves and announces a run's state
increments.goal: Give the collector an endpoint of its own that accepts a run's backlog state, keep the latest state per run, serve the runs it holds and the full state of one over its JSON API behind the existing authentication, persist it across a restart, and announce every write on the existing SSE stream.
criteria: A POST of a run's state to an endpoint of the collector's own is accepted and identified by the issue the state belongs to; a second POST for the same run replaces what was held for it, so the collector keeps the latest state per run and no history.

The JSON API answers both questions: the runs the collector holds, with what a reader needs to pick one including when each was last written, and the full state of one named run; asking for a run it does not hold answers 404.
The new ingest endpoint and the new read endpoints sit behind the collector's existing authentication and reject an unauthenticated caller exactly as its other endpoints do.
A collector restarted against the same measurement directory still serves the run state it held, persisted the way the sessions it already holds are persisted.
A write to a run's state puts a frame on the existing /api/stream SSE stream that tells an already-connected client which run changed.

tools/argus/README.md documents what the collector now accepts and serves, and tools/argus/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus/CLAUDE.md are current for the cases and modules this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
npm --prefix tools/argus test exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: Accepted at review round 0 with no findings: npm --prefix tools/argus test (179 cases, exit 0) and ./test.sh (6 suites, exit 0). It fixed the wire contract the two open increments build against: POST /api/runs with the run id and the whole backlog document, GET /api/runs listing id, issue, workflow, increment count and updatedAtMs latest-write-first, GET /api/runs/:id serving one state whole with 404 for a run not held, all behind the existing token gate, persisted as runs.jsonl and announced as an uncoalesced SSE frame naming the run and its update time. Merged into claude/argus-workflow-backlog-status-nvqmvr.

increments.title: The recorder pushes the state it just wrote, best-effort and invisible
increments.goal: Make the recorder send the run's state to the configured collector after every write it makes, without changing anything an agent or a workflow sees and without ever costing a run a failure, a wait or a line of output.
criteria: init, record, branch and close each send the state they just wrote to the collector's run-state endpoint, identified by the issue the state belongs to, so a collector that receives it then serves that exact document under that issue.
The recorder stays the only writer of backlog.json and keeps its zero dependencies; no agent page and no workflow prompt changes, so how an agent calls the recorder is exactly what it is today.
The collector's address and its credential are read from the same OTLP collector environment the rest of uroboros already exports for argus, and from nowhere else.
With no collector configured in the environment, the recorder does nothing extra.

A collector that is unreachable, slow or refusing costs the recorder neither a non-zero exit nor a wait beyond a short timeout, and produces no output: the exit codes and the one confirmation line of every subcommand stay byte-identical to today's.
skills/agent-brief/assets/CLAUDE.md is current for the cases and helpers this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: Criteria sharpened by what the collector increment fixed: the send is judged by the collector serving the same document back under the issue, and the environment is named as the OTLP collector environment uroboros already exports, which is the only such environment in the repository.

return.plan:
## What gets built

One production file changes: `skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs`. After every write it
makes — `init`, `record`, `branch`, `close` — it POSTs the document it just wrote to the
configured collector, best-effort, and says nothing about it. `read` writes nothing and sends
nothing. No agent page, no workflow prompt, no SKILL.md changes: how an agent calls the
recorder is byte-for-byte what it is today.

## The collector contract, verified

`tools/argus/src/server.mjs` (already built by the collector increment) accepts
`POST /api/runs` with a JSON body `{ id?, state }`:

- `state` must be a non-array object, else 400 `{ error: 'run state required' }`.
- `id` is `payload.id` trimmed, falling back to `state.issue` trimmed; neither usable is 400.
- Authentication is the same gate as every other route: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
  (or `?token=`). Only `/api/health` is exempt.
- Body cap is 32 MB (`MAX_BODY_BYTES`), far above any backlog.json.
- The document is held opaquely; only `issue`, `workflow` and the increment count are read
  out of it.

So the recorder sends the whole backlog document as `state` and an explicit `id`, and needs
nothing else from the collector.

## The change, concretely

1. **Imports.** Keep `node:fs`; add `node:path` (stdlib, so zero dependencies still holds).
   Nothing else. The transport is the global `fetch`.

2. **Each write subcommand returns the backlog object it wrote.** `init`, `record`, `branch`
   and `close` each already hold that object when they call `writeBacklog`; make each
   `return backlog` as its last statement, after its `process.stdout.write`. `read` returns
   nothing. Keep `writeBacklog` synchronous and untouched — it stays the atomic
   `.tmp`-and-rename write.

3. **One send site, in the dispatch tail.** The `switch` assigns the returned object to a
   `state` variable; below the switch:

       if (state) await announce(state, rest[0])

   Top-level `await` in this `.mjs` is fine — verified that `node --check` (which
   `test-repo.sh` runs over this file) accepts a module with top-level await. `rest[0]` is the
   backlog path for all four write subcommands. One site means no subcommand can be added
   later that forgets to send. Every error path goes through `fail()`, which calls
   `process.exit`, so a failed call never reaches the send.

4. **The reader of the environment.** A helper that takes `process.env` as an argument (so it
   is a pure function and could be exercised directly later) and returns `null` or
   `{ url, authorization }`:

   - Address: `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` first, `UROBOROS_OBS_URL` second; each trimmed,
     empty treated as absent, trailing slashes stripped. `null` when neither is set — that is
     the "no collector configured, do nothing extra" case, and it costs no syscall.
   - Endpoint path: the base plus `/api/runs`.
   - Credential: parse `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` as the comma-separated `key=value` list
     the OTLP convention defines, take the value of the case-insensitively matched
     `authorization` key verbatim (argus writes exactly `Authorization=Bearer <token>`);
     failing that, `UROBOROS_OBS_TOKEN` non-empty becomes `Bearer <token>`; failing that, no
     authorization header.

   Both name pairs come out of one place, `otelEnvFor` in `tools/argus/src/claude.mjs`, which
   sets `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`/`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` and then the same address
   and secret again as `UROBOROS_OBS_URL`/`UROBOROS_OBS_TOKEN` — the names its own commands
   and argus-ui read. So reading both pairs is still "the same OTLP collector environment and
   nowhere else": no flag, no config file, no new variable, no default address. The OTLP pair
   wins when both are set, since it is the block a measured session always carries.

5. **The send.** An `async function announce(state, backlogPath)` whose whole body sits in one
   `try` with an empty `catch`:

   - Return immediately if `typeof fetch !== 'function'` (a Node too old to have it) or if the
     environment names no collector.
   - Identity: `state.issue` trimmed when it is a non-empty string, else
     `path.dirname(backlogPath)` — the issue directory the state was written into. Send it as
     `id` explicitly rather than leaning on the collector's own fallback, so a state whose
     `issue` is empty is still filed under something a reader recognises.
   - `fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify({ id, state }),
     signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2000) })` with `content-type: application/json` and the
     authorization header when there is one.
   - Ignore the answer entirely: no status check, no body read, no log, no rethrow. A non-2xx
     is as silent as a success.

   2000 ms is the short timeout. It is a constant at the top of the file, not configurable —
   configurability would be a second place the environment is read.

## Why this shape, and what I rejected

- **Measured, not assumed:** on Node v22.22.2 a `fetch` bounded by `AbortSignal.timeout`
  costs a refused connection 4 ms, a DNS failure 6 ms, and a server that accepts and never
  answers exactly the timeout (1504 ms for a 1500 ms bound) — and the process exited 0 ms
  after the last await in every case, with the response body never read. So `fetch` neither
  hangs the recorder on undici keep-alive nor needs an explicit drain. This is why the plan
  does not reach for `node:http`.
- **Rejected: fire-and-forget over `node:http` with an unref'd socket.** It would let the
  process exit before the request is even flushed, so a local collector would usually receive
  nothing — the first criterion asks that the collector then serves that exact document.
- **Rejected: awaiting the send inside `writeBacklog`.** It would delay the confirmation line
  by up to the timeout. Printing first and sending after keeps the visible behaviour identical
  in time as well as in bytes.
- **Rejected: a detached child process to do the send.** A process per write, unbounded, and
  untestable.
- **Rejected: retries.** Best-effort means one attempt; the next write resends the whole
  document anyway, since every send carries the complete state rather than a delta.
- **Rejected: a new variable such as UROBOROS_BACKLOG_COLLECTOR, a CLI flag, or a default
  localhost address.** Each would be a second source of the address, which the criterion
  forbids; a default address would also make "no collector configured" impossible.
- **Rejected: sending only a diff, or only on `close`.** The criterion names all four writes,
  and the collector keeps the latest document per run with no history to merge into.

## What must not change

The four confirmation lines stay exactly:

    wrote <backlogPath> with <n> increment(s)
    recorded <label>
    recorded branch <branchName> on <incrementId>
    closed <incrementId> as <status>

one line each, on stdout, before the send. Nothing new is ever written to stdout or stderr.
Exit codes stay 0 on success, 1 for "the state says no", 2 for "you called it wrong".

## Documentation

Only `skills/agent-brief/assets/CLAUDE.md` changes, and it is the test-author's to update as
the suite doc. Do not touch `skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md` or any agent page: the criterion
forbids it, and the call is unchanged anyway. The new behaviour is explained in
`backlog.mjs`'s own header comment instead — say there that the send is best-effort, that it
is silent by design, where the address and credential come from, and that the recorder is
still the only writer of the file.

Gains node:path, a collector-from-environment reader, an async announce(), a return value on each write subcommand, and an awaited send in the dispatch tail.

Gains an environment scrubber on the existing helpers plus async spawn and collector-stub helpers and the send cases.

The map is otherwise right and complete for this increment: these three files are the whole change.
Read but unchanged, and load-bearing for the plan: tools/argus/src/server.mjs (POST /api/runs takes { id?, state }, id falls back to state.issue, Bearer gate, 32 MB body cap); tools/argus/src/claude.mjs otelEnvFor (exports OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=Authorization=Bearer <token>, and the same address and secret again as UROBOROS_OBS_URL/UROBOROS_OBS_TOKEN); test-repo.sh (runs node --check over backlog.mjs and asserts test.sh lists the suite); workflows/agile-loop.js (names backlog.mjs in prompts only, never spawns it, so no workflow run is slowed by the send).
return.environment:
Node 20.11 or newer; this repository has no linter, no formatter and no build step, and every
tool in it is dependency-free, so no npm install is needed before anything below.

Both commands run from the repository root:

- node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs — the recorder's suite alone.
- ./test.sh — every suite in the repository, the recorder's among them.

The new test cases start a node:http server on 127.0.0.1 port 0 inside the test process; they
need loopback only, and no collector, no argus process and no network access. They must not
inherit a real collector from the shell: the suite scrubs OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT,
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, UROBOROS_OBS_URL and UROBOROS_OBS_TOKEN from the environment it
gives the CLI, so running the suite in a shell where argus env has been evaluated is safe.
return.testPlan:
Tests are needed. All of them live in one file — skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs —
under node:test with node:assert/strict, and the whole file is run by

    node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs

## Helpers to add first

The suite doc (skills/agent-brief/assets/CLAUDE.md) owns the conventions; these are the new
helpers this increment needs, and the doc has to gain them:

- cleanEnv(extra) — a copy of process.env with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT,
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, UROBOROS_OBS_URL and UROBOROS_OBS_TOKEN removed, then any
  `extra` merged over it. The existing run() and runFails() pass cleanEnv() as `env`, so no
  pre-existing case can reach a developer's real collector.
- collectorStub(options) — starts a node:http server on 127.0.0.1:0, records every request as
  { method, url, headers, body } (body as the raw string), answers 200 {"ok":true} by default,
  and takes an override for answering another status or never answering at all. Returns
  { url, requests, close() }. close() must call server.closeAllConnections() before
  server.close(): the never-answering case leaves a socket open, and a plain close() would
  hang the suite at exit.
- runAsync(args, env, options) — promisified execFile of process.execPath with [cli, ...args],
  encoding utf8, the given env, and a 10000 ms child timeout. It returns { stdout, stderr }.
  Every case that expects the stub to answer must use this and not the existing synchronous
  run(): execFileSync blocks the very event loop the stub answers on, so a synchronous spawn
  would make every send hit its timeout and the 200 path would never be exercised.

## Cases

Criterion: init, record, branch and close each send the state they just wrote, identified by
the issue.

1. "every write sends the document it just wrote to the collector, and read sends nothing"
   — integration, backlog.test.mjs. State: a stub answering 200; env cleanEnv({
   OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: stub.url }). Input: runAsync init, then record i1
   research:i1.0, then branch i1 some-branch, then close i1 done "accepted", then read; after
   each of the four writes read backlog.json off disk. Expected: exactly four recorded
   requests, in that order; each has method POST, url '/api/runs' and a JSON content-type;
   each body parses to { id: 'docs/issues/x', state: X } where X deep-equals the file as it
   stood right after that command (so the sent document is the post-write one and the id is
   the issue the state names); the fourth request's state shows increments[0].status 'done'
   and increments[0].steps [] — the shed is in what the collector gets; the read adds no fifth
   request.

2. "the confirmation lines and the exit codes are unchanged with a collector configured" —
   same setup as case 1, asserted inside it or as its own case: init's stdout is exactly
   'wrote ' + backlogPath + ' with 1 increment(s)\n', record's exactly 'recorded
   research:i1.0\n', branch's exactly 'recorded branch some-branch on i1\n', close's exactly
   'closed i1 as done\n', and every stderr is the empty string.

Criterion: the address and credential come from the OTLP collector environment and nowhere
else.

3. "the token in the OTLP headers variable rides as the bearer header" — env cleanEnv({
   OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: stub.url, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS: 'Authorization=Bearer
   s3cret' }); run init. Expected: one request, headers.authorization === 'Bearer s3cret'.

4. "UROBOROS_OBS_URL and UROBOROS_OBS_TOKEN configure the send when the OTLP names are absent"
   — env cleanEnv({ UROBOROS_OBS_URL: stub.url, UROBOROS_OBS_TOKEN: 'env-secret' }); run init.
   Expected: one request at '/api/runs', headers.authorization === 'Bearer env-secret'.

Criterion: with no collector configured the recorder does nothing extra.

5. "with no collector in the environment nothing is sent" — a stub is running and reachable,
   but env is cleanEnv() with all four names absent; run init then record. Expected:
   stub.requests is empty, both commands exit 0 with exactly today's confirmation lines and
   empty stderr, and backlog.json on disk carries the recorded step.

Criterion: an unreachable, slow or refusing collector costs no failure, no wait beyond a short
timeout and no output.

6. "a collector that refuses the connection costs neither the exit code nor a word of output"
   — start a stub, keep its url, close it so the port refuses; env points at that url; run
   init then record. Expected: both resolve (exit 0), stdout exactly the two confirmation
   lines, stderr empty, and backlog.json holds the step. Using a just-closed port rather than
   a fixed one keeps the case from colliding with whatever else is listening on this machine.

7. "a collector that never answers costs at most a short wait, and nothing else" — a stub
   whose handler never responds; env points at it; run record through runAsync with its 10000
   ms child timeout. Expected: the call resolves rather than rejecting with a killed child,
   exit 0, stdout exactly 'recorded research:i1.0\n', stderr empty. Assert no wall-clock
   duration: the child timeout is the only clock, and its message should say that the real
   bound is the recorder's own 2 s abort, so a recorder that waits forever fails here as a
   killed child instead of hanging the suite. Tear the stub down with closeAllConnections().

8. "a collector that refuses the state leaves the exit code and the confirmation line alone" —
   two stubs, or one stub run twice, answering 500 with a JSON error body and 401 with a
   www-authenticate header; run record against each. Expected: exit 0, stdout exactly
   'recorded research:i1.0\n', stderr empty, and the state still written to disk.

## Not tested, and why

- The exact timeout value as a number of milliseconds. A wall-clock assertion around a spawn
  measures process start and the machine's load, not the recorder — the same reason
  tools/argus/CLAUDE.md forbids one on its probe paths. Case 7 binds the behaviour that
  matters: the wait ends, well inside a bound that a hang would blow through.
- The collector actually storing and serving the pushed document. tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs
  and tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs own that, from the collector increment; asserting it here
  would couple the recorder's dependency-free suite to a tool it must not import.
- HTTPS endpoints, proxies and compressed bodies. One fetch call with no branch of its own.
- OTLP header values that are URL-encoded, and header names other than authorization. argus's
  own env block writes neither, and the criterion scopes the source to that block.
- A backlog whose `issue` is empty, falling back to the directory name for the id. It is a
  defensive path no workflow produces; the implementer's fallback is documented in the plan,
  and if the test-author wants it covered, one extra case on case 1's stub is enough.

## The suite doc

skills/agent-brief/assets/CLAUDE.md exists and is accurate about today's suite; it is the
test-author's to correct in this same commit, and one thing in it becomes wrong:

- "Faked vs real" says every case spawns backlog.mjs with execFileSync. That stays true for
  the existing cases, but the collector cases must spawn asynchronously, because a synchronous
  spawn blocks the loop the in-process stub answers on. Say both, and say why.
- "Faked vs real" must also record that the collector is a real node:http server on port 0 in
  the test process, nothing is mocked, and that run()/runFails() scrub the collector
  environment so a developer with argus env evaluated in their shell never has the suite
  talking to a real collector.
- "What the suite covers" gains the best-effort send: the four writes that send, read's
  silence, the two environment name pairs, the silence with none configured, and the exit
  codes and stdout surviving a refusing, unreachable or hanging collector.
- "Helpers and fixtures" gains cleanEnv, collectorStub and runAsync.
- "Where a new case belongs": the send cases go in a block at the end of the file, after the
  atomic-write case, since they are shared mechanics rather than one subcommand's rules.

## What is already red

I ran neither check command, and did not run any suite: a run buys no fact I could not state
from reading. I expect both green today. The one exception I did take, because the design
depended on it, was two throwaway probes in the scratchpad outside the repository, on Node
v22.22.2: node --check accepts a module with top-level await, and a fetch bounded by
AbortSignal.timeout returns in 4 ms against a refused port, 6 ms against an unresolvable host
and exactly at the timeout against a server that never answers, with the process exiting
immediately afterwards and the response body never read. The new cases 1-4 and 6-8 must fail
before the change (zero requests recorded where some are expected); case 5 passes before and
after, and is there to keep the silence from being lost later.
return.summary: The recorder gains one best-effort, silent POST of the document it just wrote to the collector named by the OTLP environment, sent from a single site in its dispatch tail and bounded by a 2 s abort, with the suite and its doc extended to cover the send, the silence and the untouched stdout and exit codes.

increments.title: argus-ui shows a run's backlog state, live and switchable
increments.goal: Give the interface a run view that shows a run's whole backlog state as the collector serves it, opens on the most recently written run, lets the reader switch runs, and updates itself over the collector's SSE stream.
criteria: The view shows, for the run it is showing: the issue and the workflow it belongs to and when it was last written; the increments in the backlog's order, each with its id, title, status, branch and note; a count of how many increments are closed and how many are open; and the codemap.

Per increment it shows the steps recorded so far, each with its label, its time and its return, collapsed to a summary line and expandable to the full return; the run's own steps — the opening cut, each close, the publish — are shown the same way.

The view opens on the run written to most recently and the reader can switch to any other run the collector holds, taking both the list of runs and the one run's whole state from the collector's run endpoints and from no other source.

A write to the shown run's state reaches an already-open page live over the collector's Server-Sent-Events stream, whose frame names only which run changed and when: no polling, no reload, no manual refresh.
A closed increment reads as closed, with its status and its note, and an increment with no steps renders as the normal state it is rather than an empty panel that looks broken.
The existing session view, its timeline and its stream handling keep working unchanged beside the new view.
argus-ui still imports nothing outside itself and reads no uroboros file; test/independence.test.mjs still guards exactly that rule, covers every module the view adds, and passes.

tools/argus-ui/README.md says what the interface now shows, and tools/argus-ui/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md are current for the cases and modules this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.

A collector restarted against the same measurement directory still serves the run state it held, persisted the way the sessions it already holds are persisted.
A write to a run's state puts a frame on the existing /api/stream SSE stream that tells an already-connected client which run changed.

tools/argus/README.md documents what the collector now accepts and serves, and tools/argus/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus/CLAUDE.md are current for the cases and modules this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
npm --prefix tools/argus test exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.

It fixed the wire contract the two open increments build against: POST /api/runs with the run id and the whole backlog document, GET /api/runs listing id, issue, workflow, increment count and updatedAtMs latest-write-first, GET /api/runs/:id serving one state whole with 404 for a run not held, all behind the existing token gate, persisted as runs.jsonl and announced as an uncoalesced SSE frame naming the run and its update time. increments.title: The recorder pushes the state it just wrote, best-effort and invisible
increments.goal: Make the recorder send the run's state to the configured collector after every write it makes, without changing anything an agent or a workflow sees and without ever costing a run a failure, a wait or a line of output.
criteria: init, record, branch and close each send the state they just wrote to the collector's run-state endpoint, identified by the issue the state belongs to, so a collector that receives it then serves that exact document under that issue.
The recorder stays the only writer of backlog.json and keeps its zero dependencies; no agent page and no workflow prompt changes, so how an agent calls the recorder is exactly what it is today.
The collector's address and its credential are read from the same OTLP collector environment the rest of uroboros already exports for argus, and from nowhere else.
With no collector configured in the environment, the recorder does nothing extra.

A collector that is unreachable, slow or refusing costs the recorder neither a non-zero exit nor a wait beyond a short timeout, and produces no output: the exit codes and the one confirmation line of every subcommand stay byte-identical to today's.
skills/agent-brief/assets/CLAUDE.md is current for the cases and helpers this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: Criteria sharpened by what the collector increment fixed: the send is judged by the collector serving the same document back under the issue, and the environment is named as the OTLP collector environment uroboros already exports, which is the only such environment in the repository.

increments.title: argus-ui shows a run's backlog state, live and switchable
increments.goal: Give the interface a run view that shows a run's whole backlog state as the collector serves it, opens on the most recently written run, lets the reader switch runs, and updates itself over the collector's SSE stream.
criteria: The view shows, for the run it is showing: the issue and the workflow it belongs to and when it was last written; the increments in the backlog's order, each with its id, title, status, branch and note; a count of how many increments are closed and how many are open; and the codemap.

Per increment it shows the steps recorded so far, each with its label, its time and its return, collapsed to a summary line and expandable to the full return; the run's own steps — the opening cut, each close, the publish — are shown the same way.

The view opens on the run written to most recently and the reader can switch to any other run the collector holds, taking both the list of runs and the one run's whole state from the collector's run endpoints and from no other source.

A write to the shown run's state reaches an already-open page live over the collector's Server-Sent-Events stream, whose frame names only which run changed and when: no polling, no reload, no manual refresh.
A closed increment reads as closed, with its status and its note, and an increment with no steps renders as the normal state it is rather than an empty panel that looks broken.
The existing session view, its timeline and its stream handling keep working unchanged beside the new view.
argus-ui still imports nothing outside itself and reads no uroboros file; test/independence.test.mjs still guards exactly that rule, covers every module the view adds, and passes.

tools/argus-ui/README.md says what the interface now shows, and tools/argus-ui/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md are current for the cases and modules this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: Criteria sharpened by what the collector increment fixed: the run list and the one run's state come from the collector's run endpoints, and the stream frame names only the run that changed and when. One criterion added, that the existing session view keeps working, because the view switch lands in a page built for a single view.

return.summary:
Landed the collector increment and re-cut what is left. `git fetch origin claude/argus-workflow-backlog-status-nvqmvr--collector` then a merge into claude/argus-workflow-backlog-status-nvqmvr fast-forwarded with no conflict (b0b0b1e..9b870db), and the push succeeded first try. Closed `collector` as done on the review's verdict: accepted at round 0, no findings, npm --prefix tools/argus test 179 cases exit 0 and ./test.sh 6 suites exit 0.

What that increment showed, and what I changed for it. It fixed a wire contract that was a guess when I cut the plan: the collector takes the whole backlog document at POST /api/runs under an id that falls back to the issue the state names, lists runs with id, issue, workflow, increment count and last-write time newest first, serves one run whole and 404s for one it does not hold, all behind the existing token gate, persists as runs.jsonl and announces an uncoalesced SSE frame carrying only the run id and its update time. So `recorder` now says the send is judged by the collector serving the same document back under that issue, and `ui` now says the list and the one run come from those endpoints and that the stream frame names only which run changed and when. The researcher also proved the environment question answerable without a human: the OTLP collector environment (endpoint plus headers) is the only collector environment in the repository, so `recorder`'s criterion names it instead of leaving it open, and no question goes to the human.

I added one criterion to `ui`: the existing session view, its timeline and its stream handling keep working beside the new one. The page is built for a single view and the run view arrives with a switch, so that is the thing most likely to break silently and the thing no other criterion covers.

What I did not change. The order stands: `recorder` then `ui`. Both now depend only on a contract that is fixed and merged, so neither blocks the other; `recorder` is the smaller and closes the write path while the contract is fresh, and `ui` — the largest, the one most likely to need re-cutting — goes last, where a re-cut costs least of the six increments still in budget. I considered splitting `ui` into a rendered view and a live, switchable one, and rejected it: the static half is a page nobody asked for, and the interface's one-module-one-suite rule means both halves land in the same new module and the same new suite. Three criteria of the issue that had no home in the collector increment sit in `ui` and nowhere else: that argus-ui imports nothing outside itself, that the interface documentation is current, and that ./test.sh is green — each increment carries its own ./test.sh line, which is the one criterion the issue repeats by design.

Codemap changes. The collector's nine files move to a trailing paragraph as already changed, so a researcher reads them as the contract rather than as work. Two new lines: a run-view module under tools/argus-ui/public/ and its suite under tools/argus-ui/test/, because the interface's conventions page requires one suite per module and the view will not fit in app.js; naming them is the researcher's. Four entries are recorded as deliberately absent, each checked: tools/argus/bin/argus.mjs and tools/argus/src/config.mjs (run state rides --persist and --open untouched), tools/argus-ui/src/server.mjs (its reverse proxy already forwards everything under /api/, streams piped not buffered), and skills/argus/SKILL.md plus the workflow and agent pages (the issue forbids changing how an agent calls the recorder).
